images.prompt: Create a high resolution landscape 2 by 2 equal-panel educational botanical illustration sheet for a Chinese tea book. No text, no labels, no logos. Ivory background, restrained realistic gouache and extremely crisp macro leaf detail. Each panel isolated with wide straight cream gutters. TOP LEFT: a fresh Camellia sinensis shoot lying flat, one slender unopened pale green terminal bud and two distinctly separate tender lanceolate green leaves attached to the same stem; show fine serrated margins, midrib and lateral veins, subtle tiny white hairs only on the bud. TOP RIGHT: side by side two detached fresh tea leaves, one small tender pale green leaf and one larger thicker dark green mature leaf; tea leaves both lanceolate with serrated edge and visible veins, no other species. BOTTOM LEFT: three separated intact freshly picked tender tea shoots gently wilted, softer drooping leaves, still green, no dried tea or blackened leaves. BOTTOM RIGHT: macro view of a fresh tea leaf with one small mechanically bruised reddish brown patch at its edge, rest green, and a second curled dried green tea leaf nearby; distinguish fresh smooth hydrated texture from dry wrinkled texture. No arrows, no invented microscopic structures, no tea cups. Objects fit entirely in each panel with generous padding. Accurate botanical teaching illustration rather than photographic evidence; uniform overhead view and lighting.

images.purpose: 六类代表形态的干茶与叶底对照；不作为样本证据
images.prompt: High resolution educational tea specimen illustration sheet, exactly SIX equal rectangular panels in TWO COLUMNS and THREE ROWS, wide ivory gutters. Landscape canvas. Each panel has TWO clearly separated specimen groups: LEFT a small cluster of dry processed tea, RIGHT three or four of the SAME representative tea's brewed wet expanded leaves laid flat individually. NO tea cups, NO text, NO labels, NO arrows, NO flowers, no logos. Extremely crisp macro botanical detail in realistic restrained gouache, consistent neutral daylight overhead specimen view, cream background. Reading order: TOP LEFT green tea represented by Longjing: dry flat pale olive green pressed sword-shaped leaves; wet flat tender yellow-green narrow leaves and buds. TOP RIGHT white tea represented by Bai Mudan: dry naturally spread gray green leaves with silvery hairy pointed buds and small stems; wet expanded olive green leaves with pale buds, natural lightly browned edges. MIDDLE LEFT yellow tea represented by Junshan Yinzhen: dry straight stout slender buds of pale yellow olive gold with subtle white fuzz; wet slightly plumper pale yellow green buds, NOT large unfolded mature leaves. MIDDLE RIGHT oolong represented by rolled Taiwan style oolong: dry tightly rolled uneven dark olive balls with leaf texture (NOT pellets/seeds); wet clearly expanded broad olive green leaves with subtle reddish brown margins, small stems. BOTTOM LEFT Chinese black tea hongcha represented by orthodox rolled leaf black tea: dry twisted dark brown slender strips with a few golden tips; wet unfolded copper brown leaves, softly wrinkled. BOTTOM RIGHT dark postfermented tea represented by ripe Pu-erh loose leaf: dry thick irregular dark reddish brown strips and tiny stems; wet dark brown expanded soft leaf pieces with visible veins, NOT green leaves. Every panel must show both dry and wet groups at large magnification, ample internal margins, botanical textures distinctly legible, no decorations. These are representative teaching examples, not photographic evidence or grade certification.
